g1.label: 1. There is ___ milk
g1.why: "Milk" is uncountable, so it cannot take "many" or "a few". "Some" works with uncountable nouns in a positive sentence.

g2.label: 2. there aren't ___ eggs
g2.why: "Eggs" is countable (one egg, two eggs). Use "many" in a negative sentence with a countable noun.

g3.label: 3. How ___ bread
g3.why: "Bread" is uncountable. In a "How … ?" question, use "much" with uncountable nouns.

g4.label: 4. Only ___
g4.why: "Bread" is uncountable, so use "a little", not "a few". "A little" means a small amount, but enough.

g5.label: 5. ___ drinks
g5.why: "Drinks" is countable. "A lot of" works with countable and uncountable nouns; "much" is unusual in a positive sentence, and "a little" is only for uncountable nouns.

g6.label: 6. How ___ bottles
g6.why: "Bottles" is countable (one bottle, two bottles). In a "How … ?" question, use "many".

g1.label: 1. How ___ water
g1.why: "Water" is uncountable: you cannot count "one water, two waters" as a substance. Use "much".

g2.label: 2. aren't ___ chairs
g2.why: "Chairs" is countable. Use "many" in a negative sentence.

g3.label: 3. How ___ students
g3.why: "Students" is countable (one student, two students). Use "many".

g4.label: 4. don't have ___ time
g4.why: "Time" is uncountable here. Use "much" in a negative sentence.

g5.label: 5. Is there ___ sugar
g5.why: "Sugar" is uncountable. Use "much" in a question.

g6.label: 6. haven't got ___ apples
g6.why: "Apples" is countable. Use "many" in a negative sentence.

g7.label: 7. How ___ people
g7.why: "People" is countable (one person, two people). Use "many".

g8.label: 8. doesn't eat ___ meat
g8.why: "Meat" is uncountable. Use "much" in a negative sentence.

g1.label: 1. I have ___ time
g1.why: "Little" + an uncountable noun means almost none, which fits "I can't talk now".

g2.label: 2. ___ sugar
g2.why: "A little" + an uncountable noun means a small amount. "Just a spoonful" shows the amount is small but welcome.

g3.label: 3. He has ___ friends
g3.why: "Few" + a countable noun means almost none, which fits "he often feels lonely". "A few" would be positive.

g4.label: 4. We have ___ eggs
g4.why: "A few" + a countable noun means some, enough to do something. It fits "I can make an omelette".

g5.label: 5. ___ people came
g5.why: "Few" + a countable noun means almost none, which fits "the hall was nearly empty".

g6.label: 6. ___ advice
g6.why: "Advice" is uncountable, so use "a little", not "a few". It asks for a small amount.

g7.label: 7. ___ apple
g7.why: Recall from the Articles page: "apple" starts with a vowel sound, so use "an". "Bread" is uncountable, so it takes "some", not "a".

g8.label: 8. ___ time before the film
g8.why: "Time" is uncountable and positive here: there is some, enough for a coffee. Use "a little".
